rawFindings.title: Incorrect Windows absolute path detection for ':' drive letter paths
rawFindings.explanation: The original code checked for a Windows device path by testing if the second character of the path is ':' and the third character is either a backslash '\' or a forward slash '/'. The fix changes this to only accept a backslash '\' after ':'. This causes paths like 'c:/' to no longer be detected as absolute, since they use forward slash. This breaks detection of valid absolute Windows paths using forward slashes (which Windows supports).
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original check to allow either '\' or '/' after the colon to properly detect Windows absolute paths using either slash as separator.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect Windows device path absolute check ignoring forward slashes
rawFindings.explanation: The original code considered paths like 'C:/foo' as absolute (Windows device path), by checking if path[1] is ':' and path[2] is either '\' or '/'. The changed code removes the check for '/'. This causes 'C:/' (and similarly 'C:/anything') not to be recognized as absolute paths on Windows, which is incorrect since Windows supports both backslash and forward slash as path separators.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the check to include both '\\' and '/' as valid separators at path[2] for Windows device paths: if (':' === path[1] && ('\\' === path[2] || '/' === path[2])) return true;

rawFindings.title: Incorrect Windows absolute path detection in utils.isAbsolute
rawFindings.explanation: The previous implementation of isAbsolute() accepted Windows device paths with either backslash or forward slash after the drive letter (e.g., 'c:\' or 'c:/') as absolute paths. The change restricts the detection to only backslash (\) after the drive letter, thus ignoring valid absolute Windows paths that use forward slashes (e.g., 'c:/'). Removing the test for forward slash also removes a test case in test/utils.js that checked 'c:/'. This may break code that expects paths with forward slashes
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the check for forward slash after the drive letter in isAbsolute() to correctly identify Windows absolute paths using either backslash or forward slash. Also, reinstate the relevant test case to verify both forms.
